edges.mode_basis: linked text F10 credits the dense film (sealing) and Ta corrosion resistance together; no caption or figure weighs one against the other
same sentence (linked text F10): sealing and inert Ta2O5 chemistry act together

notes: Single main line: porous MAO on AZ31 -> ALD Ta2O5 (500 cycles) -> Ta-O film covering the MAO and closing its pores -> barrier (MEC) -> ~2.7-decade lower icorr and ~2.4-decade higher |Z| -> low steady HER and intact surface over 294 h. Ta2O5 chemistry and sealing are joint causes of the corrosion gain (paper states both). Side: amorphous-Ta2O5 claim (XRD absence cannot separate amorphous from too thin), residual N from precursor (assignments doubtful: N-C at 283.0 eV below C-C), cycle sweep 500 vs 1000 (thickness argued from 0.1 nm/cycle), local pitting with nano-gap mechanism as the stated limitation, comparison with four MAO/organic composites (this paper's MAO baseline is 3-4x worse than same-group AZ31 baselines). Audit: o13, early HER of MAO/Ta2O5 barely below MAO despite the ~2.7-decade icorr gap. F9c shows no Ca map although the text says Ca was not detected. Table 1 not in packet.
